thread.title: US Dollar to Pound Exchange Rate Declines as US Charges Huawei

author: James Elliot
title: US Dollar to Pound Exchange Rate Declines as US Charges Huawei
text:
US Dollar To Pound Exchange Rate Declines As US Charges Huawei US Dollar To Pound Exchange Rate Declines As US Charges Huawei Posted by James Elliot in USD , and modified 29 Jan 2019 14:05
- Huawei Charges in the US Put a Negative Slant on this Week’s Important US-China Trade Talks
- The timing of the Huawei charges couldn’t be worse as high level trade talks get underway on Wednesday.
- China and the trade war is at the heart of the global slowdown and it is starting to show in US corporate earnings.
- This week’s Fed meeting won’t feature a rate hike, but there is plenty at stake.
Market risks are rising this week as a busy schedule of data releases and events keep traders on their toes. Equities fell on Monday and are back in the red in early Tuesday trading as concerns mount over the trade talks between the US and China due to start on Wednesday.
“Overnight, the US filed criminal charges against Huawei and its CFO Meng Wanzhou, accusing the Chinese telecom company of stealing American technology and breaking US sanctions against Iran. The allegations weighed on Asian markets this morning, with technology stocks taking a hit, and it might complicate a pivotal round of trade talks scheduled to take place between the US and China from tomorrow,” reported Danske bank in its morning note.
Technology stocks – once the out-performing market leaders in the uptrend – are trading heavily and China seems to be the main reasons for most of the woes. Chip make Nvidia (NVDA) lowered guidance yesterday and blames deteriorating macro conditions, particularly in China, for customers delaying orders. The stock fell around -15%. Caterpillar (CAT) was also down around -10% on earnings, again attributing most of the weakness to China and the trade war. This a theme that looks set to continue through earnings season, and whether or not China is responsible for all the negatives, it is a convenient excuse for CEOs who can shift most of the blame onto something out of their control. Heavyweights Apple (AAPL), Facebook (FB) and Amazon (AMZN) also report this week, but only Apple has any real connection to China. Eyes on the Fed
As well as high level trade talks, the markets are looking ahead to the Fed meeting on Wednesday. A rate hike is not expected, but there is plenty to be cleared up around the pace (or pause) of future hikes. The market consensus is very mixed so the reaction could go either way. Here’s ING’s view,
“After December’s rate hike, the Federal Reserve indicated it would slow the pace of interest rate rises in 2019. While financial markets are not pricing in a single hike, we still think the strong jobs market and rising core inflation pressures will generate two moves later this year.”
The issue is whether the Fed will commit anything in Wednesday’s meeting or whether it will just signal a vaguely dovish stance and buy itself some time. The slowing growth narrative means it can keep the line that it is data dependent, but it does seem the recent dovish shift was also an attempt to save equities from a crash in late December. Now that they have recovered around half of the falls, perhaps the Fed will shift slightly hawkish again? After all, the economy is still strong, as ING points out,
“We agree that the economy will slow in 2019 but still forecast GDP growth of 2.3%. Moreover, given shrinking economic spare capacity and rising wages, we think core inflation pressures will be on the up, justifying further interest rate hikes – most likely in 2Q and 3Q19.”
There is also the question of whether the Fed will confirm an early end to QT as reported by the Wall Street Journal last Friday. There will be a press conference, so expect questions on this and the pace (or pause) of hikes in 2019.
There may not be a rate hike, but there is plenty potential for volatility in equities, rates and the US dollar, which has eased since the QT story and currently sits at 95.67.
